summary: A granite tower from 1856 on Rhode Island's southwest tip, replacing a wooden light of 1807-08; home of keeper Sally Ann Crandall and the Metis rescuers of 1872.

access.note: Grounds open 8 a.m. to sunset on foot via private Lighthouse Road; tower and keeper's residence closed; museum open limited summer hours.

notes_for_editor: Metis accounts conflict widely (date 29/30/31 Aug; 33 survived of 149 vs 85 rescued/67 lost vs 130 lost); no contemporary newspaper or LSS 1873 report was available in the corpus, so the story leans on the Congressional resolution text as reprinted by marinewives.com. Lighthouse Board reports before 1891 are not in the corpus; the 1855-56 construction rests on the Association, Lighthouse Friends and NRHP. Larchmont location (four miles southwest per New England Lighthouses) not checked against primary sources; it sank off Block Island by most accounts, so consider dropping. Roster line 'Myrel E. Stroud (at least 1958-)' and many USCG crew omitted from prose. Life-Saving station 1876 report is a plan, station existence cited to NEL. Roster for Wilk/Pie/Merritt: Archive says principal keeper; role set to officer in charge from NEL context. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Sally Crandall's lantern-cloth quote reworded (the source says the lantern, uncovered, might set fire); LSS 1876 report passage is about the 1850 appropriation, not a 1870s plan; Larchmont 'Providence steamer' removed (not stated by a source); 'worst night on record' replaced with Lighthouse Friends' 'two worst'.
